title: Bloom Mechanized Host Implementation Mapping V1

metadata.purpose: Technical companion to the Bloom Mechanized Host Production System V2, mapping rigid controls, sockets, five tendril chains, animation notifies, runtime ranges, collision and damage zones, VFX separation, render masks, LODs, naming, and handoff rules.
metadata.source_preservation: The selected hero concept and existing runtime prototype remain unchanged. This packet is additive and does not authorize replacement of the current host.

source_sheet.notes: Authoritative implementation companion for motion coverage, rigid hierarchy, growth sockets, spline parameters, animation notifies, runtime tuning, progression mapping, collision and damage zones, Niagara separation, material channels, render masks, LODs, naming, and handoff. The V2 master and this JSON remain authoritative where generated micro-labels are abbreviated.

master production system and visual authority

concept_source_sets.role: mechanized-host capture and quarantined reconstruction lineage

approved.value: independently articulated rigid parts under a shared native motion pivot
surface and retopology reference; never the animation source

clean image-left host structure opposed by Bloom-dominant image-right shoulder, torso, arm, and leg

conflicts.description: The selected concept contains a recessed human face and pressure-shell canopy, while the implemented prototype uses the JACK robot head with no human occupant contract.
conflicts.resolution: Approve either a human-occupied mechanized host variant with a new canopy assembly or retain the JACK robot identity and revise the face treatment before modeling.

conflicts.description: The generated front, side, rear, and three-quarter views are visually coherent but are not measured orthographic projections of one modeled asset.
conflicts.resolution: Build a measured rigid-part graybox from runtime source bounds, then regenerate controlled orthographic captures from that single model.

conflicts.description: Five late-state tendrils are visually approved for this concept, but spline, collision, replication, shadow, and encounter-density budgets are not established.
conflicts.resolution: Prototype one five-chain host under representative enemy density and approve the LOD and simulation policy.

current_bounds_cm.note: Current gameplay collision only. This is not final visual mesh bounds.

pivot.rule: Use the current capsule and AttackPoseRoot ground-centered contract. Rigid host parts and growth overlays remain children of that motion hierarchy.

blender.export_policy: Export rigid host parts, infection overlays, tendril chains, sockets, and collision as independently addressable objects with one shared root.

unreal.collision: Retain the approved 68 cm radius by 145 cm half-height gameplay capsule until measured replacement bounds pass navigation and combat tests.
unreal.import_policy: Do not replace the runtime prototype, gameplay class, or current Fab sources until the host-head conflict, measured bounds, rigid hierarchy, and performance gates pass.

requirements.requirement: Rigid host parts preserve the current independent articulation and shared motion pivot.
Growth modules remain independently hideable and do not require deformation of the clean host.
Each tendril exposes root, mid, and tip controls with rest length, stiffness, damping, and collision radius.
The approved head lineage decision is applied consistently to the model, Control Rig, collision, and all views.

states.source: native body shift and striking-arm rotation
native root drop and arm slump

requirements.requirement: The heavy bruiser silhouette remains readable at 105 to 225 cm/s.
The 0.35 second attack telegraph remains visible with reduced VFX quality.
Five tendrils do not penetrate the canopy, clean limbs, floor, or each other in representative motion.
Core, telegraph, death burst, tendril emission, and ambient particles remain independently scalable.
Enemy-state VFX never reveal whether a player-facing Bloom warning is genuine or false.
Export root socket, rest length, radius, stiffness, damping, target mode, collision mode, shadow mode, and LOD visibility for each tendril.

passes.usage: rigid motion and tendril temporal QA

requirements.requirement: Host, infection, tendrils, cores, glass, and occupant are independently selectable and maskable.
LOD transitions preserve the one-sided mass and five-tendril late-state silhouette.
One data asset maps infection phase to growth visibility, tuning, materials, VFX, tendril count, and collision policy.
The clean host remains reusable beneath separately controlled infection, core, tendril, and VFX layers.
The current runtime class and Fab prototype remain available until a measured replacement passes parity tests.
A production model is captured from one asset for front, side, rear, and three-quarter verification before visual promotion.

acceptance_checks.requirement: The packet maps to the implemented ABloomMechanizedEnemy class.
The user-selected hero concept is preserved as a separate exact-hash source.
Approve the recessed human canopy or the existing JACK robot head as the production host identity.
Replace generated view proposals with orthographic captures from one measured graybox.
Clean host, canopy, occupant, infection, cores, five tendrils, collision, and VFX can be controlled independently.
Idle, attack windup, recovery, death slump, and progression preserve current gameplay timing and collision.
Five chains pass collision, replication, shadow, LOD, and encounter-density budgets.
Character art and gameplay approve the final modeled silhouette, materials, face treatment, and progression read.

build_questions: Is this a human-occupied mechanized host variant or a visual replacement for the current JACK robot host?
Which of the five tendrils are cosmetic, query-only, or gameplay-active?
Should the cyan core nodes remain visible through every phase or only during telegraph and damage windows?
What measured visual bounds and mass should replace the current collision-only capsule record?
